A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and all your traffic goes through it.

Normally, websites see your real address, and the network you're on (café Wi-Fi, your internet provider) can see which sites you visit. With a VPN, your data is scrambled before it leaves your device. It travels to the VPN company's computer, which unscrambles it and passes it on to the website. The website sees the VPN's address, not yours.

So it hides what you do from the network around you and hides where you are from websites. It doesn't make you anonymous: the VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
